papers.title: Physics-guided surrogate learning enables zero-shot control of turbulent wings
papers.abstract: Turbulent boundary layers over aerodynamic surfaces are a major source of aircraft drag, yet their control remains challenging due to multiscale dynamics and spatial variability, particularly under adverse pressure gradients. Reinforcement learning has outperformed state-of-the-art strategies in canonical flows, but its application to realistic geometries is limited by computational cost and transferability. Here we show that these limitations can be overcome by exploiting local structures of wall-bounded turbulence. Policies are trained in turbulent channel flows matched to wing boundary-layer statistics and deployed directly onto a NACA4412 wing section at $Re_c=2\times10^5$ without additional training on the wing, constituting zero-shot deployment. The transferred policies reduce total drag by 11.1\%, while state-of-the-art opposition control reduces it by 8.9\%. With the actuation cost taken into account, the corresponding net-energy savings are 10.9\% and 8.8\%, respectively. Surrogate training provides an estimated improvement of four orders of magnitude in exploration efficiency over direct on-wing training, enabling scalable flow control.

papers.title: Fast localized urban microclimate emulator: wind and temperatures in unseen urban morphologies
papers.abstract: Urban microclimate, encompassing wind and temperature fields shaped by building geometry, strongly affects building energy use, pedestrian wind comfort, pollutant dispersion, the urban heat island, and public health. Conventional Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is computationally prohibitive for rapid assessments, while many deep learning approaches require extensive training data and struggle with generalization to unseen configurations. In this work, we present the Fast Localized Urban Microclimate Emulator (FLUME), a rapid, data-efficient, and geometry-aware framework based on a Fourier neural operator for predicting three-dimensional wind and temperature fields. FLUME assumes that, under prescribed inflow and thermal forcing, much of the spatial variation of these mean fields is controlled by surrounding building geometry. The framework introduces a Multi-Directional Distance Feature (MDDF), which captures geometry over adaptive, visibility-defined spatial scales. By decomposing simulations of only 23 urban blocks into smaller 3D patches enriched with precomputed MDDF information, FLUME enables learning from limited CFD data. The model achieves mean absolute errors of 0.2 m/s for streamwise velocity and 0.19$^{\circ}$C for temperature on unseen urban configurations. A deep ensemble provides a practical proxy for epistemic uncertainty, and conformal prediction transforms these estimates into calibrated prediction intervals. Ensemble spread is positively related to local prediction error, with greater uncertainty in roof-level shear layers, building wakes, and vertical velocity near the ground. These results indicate FLUME's potential for rapid scenario assessment in urban design and urban climate studies.

papers.title: The binormal flow: a toy model for turbulence
papers.abstract: These notes summarize the content of a one-week course given by Luis Vega on the binormal flow model applied to describe the dynamics of three-dimensional vortex filaments in incompressible fluids following the Euler equations. This topic touches connections between the binormal flow, the Schr\"odinger map and the 1d cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, providing a rich casuistry linked to the physical and numerical phenomenology. This course was part of the $2^{\text{nd}}$ Advanced Summer School held at the Institut d'Etudes Scientifiques de Carg\`ese (IESC), at Carg\`ese (Corsica), from $20^{\text{th}}$ to $30^{\text{th}}$ June 2023. These notes have been written and completed by two of its attendees, Elena Danesi and Pablo Merino.

papers.title: An Omni-Temporal Framework for Hydrodynamic Dispersion and Reaction in Porous Media
papers.abstract: Many applications involve porous-media transport driven on time scales comparable to the pore-scale diffusion time, for which classical pseudo-steady dispersion models based on time-invariant transport coefficients may become inaccurate. While frequency-dependent dispersion has been studied in non-reactive porous media, a corresponding framework that simultaneously accounts for advection, diffusion, and heterogeneous interfacial reaction remains lacking. We address this gap by introducing an omni-temporal framework based on volume averaging of the frequency-domain pore-scale advection-diffusion equation subject to a Robin boundary condition spanning the full range of interfacial reactivity. The resulting upscaled formulation yields four frequency-dependent transfer functions: a dispersion tensor, an advection-suppression vector, a spectral Sherwood number, and a reactivity-bias vector, with the reactivity-bias vector introduced here for the first time. Analytical solutions for fully developed flow between parallel plates and through circular tubes reveal distinct kinetics- and diffusion-limited regimes, including capacitive and semi-infinite Warburg-type frequency responses. Comparisons of transient breakthrough curves with direct numerical simulations demonstrate substantial improvement over conventional pseudo-steady dispersion, particularly for short-duration pulses. Application to a periodic array of square rods under cross flow further demonstrates the frameworks applicability beyond canonical geometries.

papers.title: Shear-driven arrest of dip-coating film entrainment
papers.abstract: A plate withdrawn from a bath of partially wetting liquid entrains a film above a critical velocity. Here, we show that this critical threshold can be substantially increased by the presence of a laminar gas flow opposed to the plate velocity that exerts a tangential shear stress on the liquid-gas interface. Using two-phase immiscible Navier-Stokes simulations and confining the gas to a narrow channel, we derive a closed-form expression for the interfacial stress, which combined with lubrication theory relates the thickness of the film and the contact line velocity to the applied shear stress. As the gas velocity is increased, the film thins and the contact line velocity slows down, until the imposed shear overcomes the drag of the moving plate and entrainment is arrested. As in the quiescent case, the velocity mismatch between plate and contact line is independent of the plate velocity and is set by the applied shear alone. We find that one set of varying gas flow simulations, with constant critical plate velocity, therefore determines the critical gas flow for every smaller plate velocity.

papers.title: Predicting the Final Stationary State of Sheared 2D Euler Fluids
papers.abstract: The Kelvin-Helmholtz (KH) instability is a fundamental signature of the natural world, manifesting in phenomena ranging from atmospheric clouds to the iconic turbulence of Jupiter's Great Red Spot. While the linear dynamics of this instability is well-understood, the ultimate fate of the fluid --- the final stationary state to which it relaxes --- remains a formidable challenge. In this paper, we present a general non-equilibrium statistical mechanics framework that allows us to predict the asymptotic vorticity distribution of a sheared 2D Euler fluid. By constructing a self-consistent ansatz for the solution of the Vlasov equation, we determine the stationary stream function without explicitly solving the time-dependent Euler equations. We demonstrate that the relaxation leads to a population-inverted core, where high-energy states are fully occupied, surrounded by a tenuous halo of vortices in the lower-energy regions of configuration space. This result establishes the core-halo structure as a robust statistical consequence of the system's evolution, offering a universal framework for understanding the saturation of shear-induced turbulence in inviscid 2D fluids.

papers.title: Early-time dynamics of the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability at Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic interfaces
papers.abstract: The Richtmyer-Meshkov instability (RMI) is initiated when a shock wave interacts with a perturbed interface between two materials, imparting an initial velocity to the interfacial perturbation. When the materials are viscoelastic, the subsequent evolution is influenced by the coupled effects of inertia, viscous dissipation, and elastic resistance. The interplay of these effects remains poorly understood and is important for predicting the dynamic response of shock-loaded soft materials, e.g., in blast-induced injury. Using the incompressible Cauchy momentum equation with a Kelvin-Voigt constitutive model, we conduct a linear stability analysis for the early-time post-shock evolution of a single-mode interface perturbation of two viscoelastic materials. We derive an implicit dispersion relation for the temporal growth rates of the perturbation. This relation depends on density, viscosity, and elasticity contrasts between the two materials and an viscoelastic parameter which is a bounded ratio of the viscous dissipation and elastic resistance response rates. Four material cases, spanning symmetric to highly contrasted interfaces, are examined to show how the viscoelastic number affects the growth rate structure as complex-dominated (oscillatory) or real-dominated (monotonic relaxation). The critical viscoelastic number separates these two regimes and is primarily governed by the density and viscosity contrasts. These results provide a theoretical criterion for predicting the early-time response of shock-driven interfaces involving fluids and viscoelastic solids.

papers.title: Conjugate heat transfer in turbulent pipe flow with azimuthally non-uniform heating
papers.abstract: Turbulent conjugate heat transfer (CHT) in pipes with azimuthally non-uniform heating is studied theoretically and numerically with a focus on low-$\mathrm{Pr}$ fluids. While the influence of the solid properties is well documented for uniform heat flux, their effect under azimuthally non-uniform heating has not been explored systematically. We address this gap by combining spectral analysis of the problem -- which reduces arbitrary boundary conditions to a discrete set of azimuthal wavenumbers -- with well-resolved numerical simulations of thermally and hydraulically fully developed turbulent pipe flow at $\mathrm{Re}_\tau \approx 180$ for $\mathrm{Pr} = \{0.025, 0.71\}$, representative of liquid metals and air. Two principal results emerge: (i) the global Nusselt number is independent of the azimuthal heat-flux distribution and exhibits only a minor dependence on the solid properties, resolving an open question for low-Prandtl-number fluids; (ii) CHT nevertheless strongly affects the azimuthally resolved mean temperature at low $\mathrm{Pr}$, where azimuthal conduction in the solid homogenises the interface heat flux, and governs the level of temperature fluctuations through the effusivity ratio (thermal activity ratio) $K$. Finally, an analysis of the turbulent Prandtl number $\mathrm{Pr}_{t}$ shows a strong anisotropy, particularly near the wall, and a dependence on the azimuthal wavenumber.

papers.title: Non intrusive parametric Reduced Order Models based on physics for incompressible flow
papers.abstract: Reduced order modeling provides an efficient alternative to high fidelity simulations for the rapid prediction of fluid flows in many query settings. Among non intrusive approaches, Operator Inference (OpInf) enables the identification of reduced dynamical operators directly from data while preserving a prescribed mathematical structure. The present work extends physics structured OpInf to the construction of parametric Reduced Order Models for transient incompressible flows governed by the Navier-Stokes equations. The velocity and pressure fields are represented using separate global reduced bases, and their reduced operators are identified directly from temporal and parametric POD coefficients. The identification procedure is formulated as a sequence of uncoupled least squares problems, leading to an efficient offline stage while avoiding the explicit projection of the governing equations. The approach is first evaluated on a lid driven cavity flow in a periodic regime to assess temporal extrapolation and prediction at previously unseen parameter values. Its applicability is then demonstrated for transient flow through a porous medium with a square obstacle, for which the nonlinear terms are not directly amenable to a standard Galerkin projection. The results demonstrate that the approach can accurately reproduce both velocity and pressure fields while providing computationally efficient predictions for unseen parameter values.

papers.title: Re-emergence of fingering in solidifying liquid-metal drops
papers.abstract: Solidification is expected to suppress fingering by removing mobile liquid. Here we report an unexpected re-emergence of fingering in impacting molten-tin drops: cooling first weakens peripheral fingers, but stronger undercooling restores them. At weak undercooling, fingers originate from a decelerating liquid rim and solidification reduces the effective acceleration that drives Rayleigh--Taylor-like amplification. At strong undercooling, solidification structures develop while liquid is still spreading, creating lateral mobility contrasts that redirect the residual flow. Comparison between the kinematically estimated solidification time and the experimentally measured fingering-onset and growth-termination times reveals a reversal in temporal ordering across the temperature range. A physics-based reduced-order model combines solidification-modified rim deceleration with mobility-gradient growth, captures the characteristic onset dynamics and accounts for the final finger length within the same physical framework.These findings establish solidification as an active means of regulating interfacial flow and morphology, with broad implications spanning metal-based additive manufacturing and debris mitigation in semiconducting industry.

papers.title: Particle dynamics in a microfluidic T-junction vortex flow: the role of history force
papers.abstract: The motion of inertial particles suspended in a carrier fluid, together with the dynamics of the underlying vortical structures, is investigated in a square microfluidic T-junction. The coherent structures forming near the branching strongly affect the particle distribution and may promote particle trapping around the T-region. Single-phase numerical simulations of the unperturbed base flow are combined with integration of the particle force balance equation, which, unlike most previous studies, includes the Basset-Boussinesq (BB) history force. The flow topology is analysed for $Re=500$ and $570$, while particle properties are varied through the Stokes number $St$ and the particle-to-fluid density ratio $\rho$. At $Re=500$ the base flow exhibits a steady vortex pair, whereas at $Re=570$ a Hopf bifurcation gives rise to a helical oscillation of the primary vortex pair characterized by periodic breathing. The BB history force has a non-negligible impact over the whole range of $(\rho, St)$ pairs investigated. It acts as an additional viscous force which, together with the drag of the relative motion, opposes the pressure-gradient force, widening particle spiral trajectories radially and elongating them axially. Its inclusion reduces the basin of attraction, indicating that memory effects promote particle displacement away from the vortex core and weaken trapping. At $Re=570$, spectral proper orthogonal decomposition characterizes the breathing of the primary vortex pair. Particles injected at a given location interact with the vortical structure at different phases of the cycle depending on the injection time, producing substantially different trajectories. This phase dependence is reflected in the shape and extent of the basin of attraction, quantified through the trapping probability over the inlet section and the probability density functions of the force components.

papers.title: An anatomically grounded human-scale steady hydraulic model of the lymphatic network
papers.abstract: The lymphatic system returns 2 to 3 L of interstitial fluid per day to the venous circulation and drains the central nervous system. Most models of lymph transport describe one lymphangion or a short chain, so they cannot show how body-wide topology, calibre hierarchy and the venous outlet set pressure and flow. We build a passive steady hydraulic model on an anatomically derived graph of the human lymphatic system, with 1010 vertices and 1126 edges expanded to 89,060 sub-edges. Radii follow a Murray cube law, derived both from minimum work and from wall-shear-stress homeostasis. Pressure and flow follow from nodal hydraulic balance over Hagen-Poiseuille conductances, with an exponential wall law, hysteretic valves, Starling leak, node retention and a Windkessel outlet. Active contraction is off, and only the inflow scale is calibrated. Two quantities that are not fitted land in clinical range at the same operating point. Radii fall inside the vessel-class range, from 1.50 mm in the thoracic duct to 0.16 mm in the cervical collectors, and pressures stay below the 50 mmHg cuff scale on all sub-edges. About 49% of the gross load is removed before the outlet, nearly independent of the outflow scale and of the outlet parameters. On the route that drains the central nervous system, 30% of the superficial cervical load reaches the vein, at 10 to 18 mmHg along a segment that cervical-scale models replace with a prescribed outlet pressure. The model is a passive whole-body baseline for contraction-driven and clinical extensions.

papers.title: An anatomically grounded human-scale dynamic model of contraction-driven lymphatic pumping
papers.abstract: Lymphangions, the valved muscular segments of lymphatic vessels, pump lymph against an adverse pressure gradient. Current models resolve this pumping in one vessel, a short chain or a regional network, and whole-body human models are passive. We extend the passive whole-body network of a companion static study to the active regime on the same anatomical graph, with intrinsic contraction, dynamic valves and a respiration-gated venous outlet on every vessel. Without fitting the waveform or the contraction amplitude, the network settles into a bounded pumping cycle at the lymphovenous junction, at a clinical pressure of 7.5 to 12.3 mmHg and a drainage of 35 to 50 mm^3/s. Respiration adds a swing of 1 to 2.5 mmHg at the junction and contraction about 1 mmHg inside the duct. Pressure generation is limited more by load than by drive, and no single contraction amplitude fits every vessel. Raising the subclavian venous pressure from 3 to 15 mmHg lifts the deep cervical node from 8.6 to 21.1 mmHg at the weakest drive, a transmission of 1.04 that falls to 0.78 at the strongest, so contraction buffers cervical drainage against venous pressure. The same solver gives the human cervical outlet pressure that cerebrospinal-fluid drainage models prescribe.

papers.title: Dynamics of fast magnetosonic wave turbulence
papers.abstract: Fast magnetosonic waves are among the fundamental oscillation modes of astrophysical plasmas. To study their dynamics, we carry out numerical simulations of the wave turbulence kinetic equation, which describes the evolution of the energy spectrum of a set of weakly nonlinear fast magnetosonic waves. This kinetic equation, which involves three-wave interactions, has recently been derived from compressible magnetohydrodynamics in the low-$\beta$ limit (Galtier 2023). It has an exact stationary solution, the Kolmogorov-Zakharov spectrum, corresponding to a direct energy cascade. Here we perform free decay simulations of the kinetic equation for which we propose a Kolmogorov-type phenomenology to explain the temporal decay laws of energy and integral length scale. In the forced simulations, we show that the cascade is in fact composed of a mixture of a forward cascade for counter-propagating waves, and a backward cascade for co-propagating waves, with the former being stronger than the latter. The Kolmogorov-Zakharov energy spectrum in $k^{-3/2}$ is found in the radial direction with an anisotropy due to the amplitude that depends on the angle relative to the strong mean magnetic field. We give the analytical expression of the Kolmogorov-Zakharov constant, which is numerically verified in the high Reynolds number limit. Our study provides a theoretical explanation for certain observations in the solar wind plasma (Zhao et al. 2022), where a regime of weak turbulence has been identified for fast magnetosonic waves, alongside a critical balance regime for strong Alfv\'en wave turbulence.

papers.title: On the ideal magnetohydrodynamic stability of the sheared-flow Z pinch
papers.abstract: Sheared-flow Z-pinch stability has previously been studied within ideal MHD primarily through growth rate calculations, which find that even trans-Alfv\'enic sheared flows apparently fail to suppress the kink instability. Here, trans-Alfv\'enic sheared flow is shown to stabilize the MHD kink but also to excite shear-driven instabilities characteristic of high-Reynolds-number supersonic flow. This distinction is evident from the dispersion relations underlying the growth rates, computed as the analytic dispersion function in the complex-frequency plane. Regularization splits this function into adiabatic and resonant parts describing how discrete modes emerge from and interact with the continuous spectrum. The Doppler-shifted flow continuum is then seen to interact with the interchange and kink instabilities in distinct ways. For interchange, the continuum overlaps the instability branch at all wavenumbers, so even sub-Alfv\'enic sheared flow stabilizes profiles modestly beyond the interchange threshold. The kink, by contrast, is shielded from the continuum by a frequency gap, and trans-Alfv\'enic flow is required to Doppler-shift the continuum into resonance with it, giving a geometric picture of the stabilization threshold. But shear-driven instabilities arise at this same threshold, including reflection modes and an acoustic kink. It is these shear-driven modes, not the original MHD instabilities, that dominate the ideal-MHD spectrum in trans-Alfv\'enic conditions. The ideal analysis thus describes the stabilization mechanism while showing that the stability of the sheared-flow Z pinch ultimately rests on non-ideal physics, such as finite orbit width and dissipation.

papers.title: An asymptotic-preserving reduced-order method for parametrised rarefied gas flow by proper generalised decomposition
papers.abstract: Modelling rarefied gas flow using the Boltzmann equation is vital in many areas. Because of the high dimensionality and coexistence of multiple characteristic scales, conventional solution strategies for this equation incur prohibitively high computational costs and are inadequate for rapid response in engineering design simulations. Based on proper generalised decomposition (PGD), we propose an a priori, asymptotic-preserving reduced-order method for the high-dimensional parameterised Shakhov kinetic model equation. Separated representations reduce the kinetic problem to a set of low-dimensional problems. We incorporate synthetic equations into the PGD iteration so that, in the hydrodynamic limit, the iteration reduces to solving the Navier-Stokes equations, whose solution naturally exhibits a low-rank structure. Furthermore, treating the rarefaction parameter as an additional coordinate yields a solution over the whole range of rarefaction in one offline computation. It enables fast online queries to any point in the parameter space. Numerical examples using this method show reasonable precision and a significant reduction in computational cost.

papers.title: Cosmic rays density fluctuations with turbulence universal spectrum -8/3
papers.abstract: An exact turbulence universal scaling law-8/3 for the density fluctuations of cosmic ray (CR) is obtained on the basis of a new analytical compressible turbulence theory and known two-fluid model of the CR dynamics. It is shown that the origin of this scaling law may be due to the breaking of the nonlinear simple waves in CR medium near the scale of their Larmor radii as for the space plasma of solar wind and magnetosheath.

papers.title: A force model for dense granular flows and particle segregation
papers.abstract: Dense granular flows are a common occurrence throughout nature and industry, but still exhibit phenomena that are not fully understood. One of these phenomena is the segregation of particles that constitute a dense granular flow, where particles separate due to differences in properties such as size and density. This work approaches segregation from a new perspective by developing a force model for a single particle based on the observation that there are two opposing drag forces acting on the particle. Validation of the model in mono-disperse flows reveals a family of velocity profiles, including a Bagnold profile. Further validation is done by comparing with known particle scaling laws in literature. The force model shows that the mechanism of segregation is always present in dense granular flows and that mono-disperse flows are a unique case where it is not distinctly visible. The insights in this paper prove a fundamental new way of thinking about dense granular flows and its individual particles, opening the field for new research directions.

papers.title: Dynamic mixed turbulence modeling using a super-resolution generative adversarial approach
papers.abstract: A dynamic mixed super-resolution model (DMSRM) for large-eddy simulations (LESs) is proposed, which combines the traditional dynamic mixed model (DMM) formulation with the generation of super-resolved velocity fields from which the subfilter-scale (SFS) stress tensor can be computed. A data-driven super-resolution generative adversarial network (SR-GAN) is employed to upsample the grid-filtered velocity fields by a factor of two, enabling the evaluation of both scale-similarity and the dynamic Smagorinsky contributions. A priori analyses of forced homogeneous isotropic turbulence (HIT) show that the SR-GAN accurately reconstructs flow features and generalizes well across different filter sizes and higher Reynolds numbers within the same flow configuration, even for unseen input fields. The DMSRM reproduces SFS stresses and energy dissipation more accurately than the traditional DMM. A posteriori LES calculations further confirm that DMSRM predicts the energy spectrum and intermittency more accurately than DMM, even for different LES grid-scale resolutions and higher Reynolds numbers than those used for training within the same forced HIT flow configuration. Unlike DMM, DMSRM yields realistic backscatter and physically consistent SFS energy dissipation. These improvements arise from the physically accurate super-resolved fields generated by the SR-GAN, from which SFS stresses are directly computed. The result is a closure that accurately reproduces stress magnitudes and dissipation while reducing reliance on additional dissipation from the dynamic term. The DMSRM formulation achieves a balance of physical fidelity, robustness, and computational efficiency, offering a promising alternative to traditional DMMs for turbulence LES modeling.

papers.title: Data-driven oscillator model for turbulent flows with multiple dominant frequencies
papers.abstract: The complex dynamics of high-dimensional oscillatory flows can be simplified using phase-reduction analysis, providing a deeper understanding of the flow response to external perturbations. Although phase-based modeling and analysis have been utilized in recent studies on oscillatory fluid flows, their usage is often limited to single-frequency flows due to difficulties in addressing chaotic characteristics, emerging from multiple dominant frequencies with broadband spectra in turbulent flows. In order to overcome this limitation, we propose a data-driven framework that models the dynamics of turbulent flows with multiple dominant frequencies based on a set of oscillators. The representative oscillators are extracted from the flow field data by training specially designed autoencoders. The oscillator dynamics are modeled through a machine-learning technique using neural networks to accurately predict the multi-frequency oscillatory behavior of turbulent flows. We verify the oscillator-based model of the oscillatory turbulent flows by applying the proposed data-driven method to the three-dimensional supersonic turbulent flow over a cavity. We show that the oscillators extracted from the spanwise-averaged pressure field represent the dominant large-scale flow features and reflect the physical characteristics of the turbulent cavity flow. The data-driven oscillator dynamics model with observation-based correction accurately forecasts the oscillatory behavior of the turbulent cavity flow for a long period. The proposed data-driven method for reduced-order modeling of turbulent flows with oscillators will enable deeper investigations of perturbation dynamics and control of turbulent flows.

papers.title: Equations of motion for dust particles in dust-collecting devices (Translated article from USSR Journal Otoplenie i Ventilyatsiya, No. 4 (1934): 27-29)
authors: L. S. Klyachko (Translators: Carlos A A. Ram{\i}rez
papers.abstract: Preface for the English Translation: While checking out early USSR journal articles for our literature search, we recently had tremendous difficulty acquiring this 1934 Klyachko original publication through our library systems. After obtaining and reading a scanned copy of it supplied by the Russian library in Moscow, we realized that relatively scarce citations of this work in the Western literature are often accompanied by inaccurate descriptions and comments, indicating that most Western authors might have gotten only second-hand knowledge about it and never seemed to have read the original article. Compared with various correlation formulas in the modern literature, the Klyachko 1934 formula for sphere drag in fluid flow appears to be the most elegant and cleanest one thus far. Therefore, we decided to make an effort to translate this historical work and publish it in the open literature to facilitate its accessibility to English readers worldwide.
